executionLog.slice: Durable per-actor native completion reservations and crash recovery
changes: Added a device-only Keychain completion journal scoped by canonical actor/organization/visit identity and checked against the original home. Hashed account keys contain no human names. Record version, UUID attempt identity, scope, revision, outcomes, monetary values and evidence IDs are validated; malformed/corrupt/oversized records fail closed rather than becoming absent.

SecItemAdd reserves a pending record without overwriting an existing one. Each reservation carries an independent attempt UUID and exact original bytes; SHA256 generic metadata constrains cleanup to that exact record. An older acknowledgment cannot target a newer reservation. The existing AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly accessibility configuration is used.

Extracted a tested journal submission pipeline: persistence must succeed before network I/O; original payload is sent; scoped completed response is required before cleanup. Network uncertainty, cancellation, wrong-home result and cleanup failures retain the original pending record. Known no-commit revision/competing-receipt conflicts resolve only their exact reservation.

Native visit reload reads the saved record only after current authorized detail succeeds, restores the original revision/outcome/notes/costs/file IDs, and freezes them for an explicit retry. executionLog.slice: Catalog revision fencing and explicit failed-quote recovery
implemented: Staged organization catalog revisions advance transactionally for all writes to 13 actual quote definition sources, including catalog prices, packages/items, configuration rules, plan/version/elevation, community offerings, incentives, feature flags and communities. Tenant moves invalidate both organizations; rolled-back source writes roll back their revisions. Truncation is refused to prevent bypass.

Revision evidence is exact positive PostgreSQL bigint text, read through a bounded org-primary-key query. Atomic pricing captures and rechecks the revision around definition reads and includes it in the reviewed quote fingerprint. Even equal-dollar definition changes require fresh review. The disabled legacy path performs no revision reads and retains its previous fingerprint inputs.

Atomic creation compares the saved quote revision while holding a shared revision lock. Referenced organization/plan/version/elevation parents are key-locked before this shared lock and definition reads use MVCC to avoid the identified row/revision inversion. This ordering is a design foundation, not independent-session deadlock or performance proof. Saved receipt recovery deliberately preserves the original reviewed quote instead of repricing.

Failed quote UI offers explicit Refresh quote while preserving configuration. Request generations prevent duplicate refreshes, stale errors or old callbacks from refreshing a newer quote; quote refresh never automatically creates an agreement.

implemented: Staged package publication RPC commits package header and complete replacement member set, catalog revision changes, audit, event and immutable request receipt in one transaction. Stable organization/request keys recover the exact saved publication without additional inserts/audits. Changed requests under the same key and changed current package contents require review. Original/current community access is reauthorized and price batch authorization is checked once per distinct community. Costs, raw request and source JSON are never returned.

Staged acknowledgment RPC requires matching committed receipt and exact original inputs, current permissions, stable acknowledgment key and reason. Event, audit and immutable reconciliation receipt commit or rollback together. Matching repeat returns the same reconciliation identity; conflicting actor/request/reason under an acknowledgment key is rejected. No package, membership, price or catalog revision is written by reconciliation.

Service validates complete reply identity and cardinality; price/package publication and inspection reuse the same canonical request builders. Missing/context-changed/denied/disabled/malformed cases fail closed. Unknown acknowledgment replies retain the saved request; repeating acknowledgment uses the same original receipt UUID as stable acknowledgment key and same recorded reason.

Shared reconciliation panel is wired into both saved price and package recovery. It checks the receipt, shows historical commit time and current source state, and explicitly acknowledges the historical commit before clearing only the exact local request under its browser lock. Not-found receipt never exposes acknowledgment. Current catalog contents are refreshed for further review. Controls are explicitly non-submit buttons inside the package form.

Parent forms only reset drafts/recovery after confirmed acknowledgment and successful exact local cleanup. Local-storage removal failure preserves recovery and allows idempotent acknowledgment retry. Current permission/feature gates disable reconciliation controls.

executionLog.slice: EP03: required durable catalog intents, bounded awaiting-outcome queues and explicit recovery retry
implemented: Added immutable organization/actor/kind/request-key intents and private active claim pointers to the staged package foundation. One unresolved request per actor/kind/scope prevents new saves from abandoning registered work; distinct kinds, actors and communities retain independent queues. Intent body, event, audit, scope counter and active claim commit atomically; audit/claim failures roll everything back.

Staged register_catalog_publication RPC reauthorizes current catalog/scope/cost access before matching private inputs, holds the same publication key lock, returns stable identity on exact replay, recognizes committed/cancelled outcomes and does not mutate catalog contents. Body/kind/actor conflicts reject. Publication and cancellation close only their matching active pointer in the outcome transaction while preserving immutable intent evidence.

Both actual Arc publishers now confirm registration before dispatching publication, preserving the identical canonical key/body. Unknown/malformed registration replies never dispatch catalog writes. After confirmed registration, rejected/uncertain publication retains an explicit recovery result so the pending intent cannot be silently abandoned. Cancelled registration blocks publication.

Closed the direct-RPC bypass: moved atomic write implementations to private contents functions denied to public/anon/authenticated/service_role. Public publication RPCs now require the original registered actor/body and matching active claim unless replaying an exact historical committed receipt. Current scope/margin access is checked before private matching; unchanged historical receipts stay replayable and changed source cannot be republished.

Extended indexed 25-row history to immutable registration events. Current awaiting requests come from the bounded claim pointer query (at most two per actor/scope), independent of old history pages. Intent outcome metadata uses only immutable receipt/cancellation sequences at the captured watermark; late outcomes do not alter earlier pages. Costs and original bodies remain absent from list metadata.

Added exact registered-intent body recovery through the same current permission, canonical body, browser-lock and verified storage path. History offers explicit retry only after receipt inspection finds no committed outcome; no automatic publication occurs. Retry uses the original request, coalesces clicks, refuses different local evidence and clears only after verified success. Confirmed resolution removes only the matching pending pointer and refreshes current history; refresh failure preserves unrelated pending work.

Fixed package success verification to compare UUID identity case-insensitively while preserving the original durable request spelling. A correct backend UUID normalization no longer falsely reports a confirmed save as unconfirmed.

Registered the new intent SQL suite in test:financials. Existing content-transaction fixtures now call the private owner kernel explicitly; strengthened ACL assertions prove service roles cannot call it, and new real service-role gateway cases prove required registration rather than weakening authorization checks.

Materialized only active claims for the actor before the immutable-intent join. executionLog.slice: EP03: actual cutoff-rule editor original review, confirmation and scoped recovery
implemented: Connected the actual CutoffRules form to separate original category review and explicit confirmation when the existing literal catalog cutover is enabled. Opening an existing rule copies its original header and complete assignment array; later catalog/row changes do not replace that source baseline. Inherited organization rules preserve their original organization scope and shared-effect explanation.

Review validates form values, invokes the authorized category review action without publishing, captures its original public definitions/hashes and creates one canonical atomic request. The shared review shows those exact definitions and original rule source. Reviewed controls freeze; returning to edits requires another explicit review and new request key. Confirm dispatches only the reviewed body, not current form/catalog values.

Confirmation acquires the original org/actor/community group browser lock and verifies exact-request storage before dispatching the existing upsert action. Every action/network failure retains evidence regardless of code. A failed storage write prevents dispatch; a failed removal after a confirmed response retains recovery. A competing tab request is preserved and promoted into the original recovery surface instead of being overwritten.

Scoped startup recovery reads the saved canonical rule request, restores its original source/scope and opens shared receipt inspection/retry/cancellation/acknowledgment. Recovery fields stay locked and there is no new-review submission. Reload recovery does not borrow current catalog defaults or silently expire a saved request. Closing recovery preserves a visible original-scope pending banner.

Epoch and current-context checks reject stale category review replies and queued confirmation callbacks after actor/permission/ambient/original scope changes, dialog cancellation or unmount. An undispatched review may close and invalidate its reply; a dispatched save cannot close away its active evidence. Duplicate review/confirmation submits coalesce. New/edit rule controls reflect pending/readiness state.

Retained legacy input behavior while the required staged migration/cutover is disabled. Existing inherited-scope/assignment regression cases explicitly exercise that legacy path, while new atomic cases cover the actual review/confirm/recovery flow.
